recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-22798. Do not change Device for this issue; any future Device FMM3 work should be handled through the later FHIR-32574 evidence and final applied/published workflow state.
issue_request: FHIR-22798 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to set the Device resource to FMM 2 based on Montreal Connectathon implementation experience and confirmation that Device, unlike DeviceDefinition, met the FMM2 criteria.
initial_application: The Jira comment records application by Jose Teixeira on 2019-07-02 in git 725e27b. That commit, "Update Device to FMM2", changed the then-authoritative [fmm] entry in source/fhir.ini from device=0 to device=2 and updated the legacy Device spreadsheet. The current source has since moved Device metadata into structuredefinition-Device.xml while preserving the FMM2 value.
additional_context: Device is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. The current [fmm] table still says device=2, the current Device StructureDefinition carries structuredefinition-fmm value 2, and the R5 published Device profile reports FMM 2. FHIR-20584 made a broader overlapping R5 FMM decision that also said Device goes to FMM2 and is already represented on the combined reconciliation branch. FHIR-32574 later records a resolved-change-required FMM3 QA decision, but it is not Applied/Published in this default run scope and remains a separate later maturity-work item.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the active current source and R5 publication surface already satisfy FHIR-22798's requested Device FMM2 outcome.

related_jiras.note: A broader Published R5 FMM issue also resolved that Device goes to FMM2 and is already represented on the combined branch.
A later Resolved-change-required issue concerns possible Device FMM3 QA and is outside this seed's applied/published FMM2 reconciliation.
A later Resolved-No-Change issue rejected moving Device maturity to normative for R5, supporting that FHIR-22798 should not be broadened beyond FMM2.
